title: Create a Claude Code Video Editing Skill for Repeatable Edits
summary: Build a repeatable Claude Code editing workflow with a manually invoked skill, per-job briefs, and plan approval. Test sample cuts before using client footage.
body_markdown:
Put the editing decisions you want to reuse in a skill, and keep this video’s footage, selects, and approved copy in a separate brief. If changing projects means opening the skill to replace filenames or timestamps, the skill is holding too much.


You'll create an` edit-review-cut` skill for your project and a brief for each video. Claude Code will propose the cut, wait for your approval, then use your available editing tools to render it.


## Separate editing rules from source choices


A reusable rule describes how you work: preserve source audio, use only supplied selects, ask before adding music or generated material, and retain the files needed to revise the edit. A job brief describes what you’re cutting today: source paths, allowed ranges, sequence, aspect ratio, and approved text.


Keep the instructions you want to reuse in the skill. Put each video’s footage and export requirements in its brief. Keep defaults in the skill and exceptions in the brief. Your usual review export might be a landscape MP4, while today’s brief asks for a portrait version. Instruct Claude Code to let the explicit job requirement override that default without changing what happens on the next job.


Keep approval and source-file handling consistent across jobs. Let the brief change the editorial choices and export settings.


You'll need a working[renderer, such as FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.html) , or a connected video editor. The skill tells Claude how to use the tools you've made available. It doesn't install them or grant permission to run them.


If the tool connection is still the problem, start with Aspect’s[existing guide to whether Claude can edit videos](https://aspect.inc/blog/post-production/can-claude-edit-videos) , or its[Claude and DaVinci Resolve guide](https://aspect.inc/blog/post-production/davinci-resolve-mcp-claude-chatgpt-codex) . Here, you need to make an already-working setup repeatable.


## Save your editing skill


From your project root, create` .claude/skills/edit-review-cut/SKILL.md` . That location and the` /edit-review-cut` command are Claude Code specific.


Set` disable-model-invocation: true` so you[start the skill yourself](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#control-who-invokes-a-skill) with` /edit-review-cut` . Claude Code's[tool permissions still apply](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#restrict-claude%E2%80%99s-skill-access) when the skill runs.


Paste this starter into` SKILL.md` . The YAML at the top belongs inside the skill file.


```text
---
name: edit-review-cut
description: Plan and render a review cut from a per-job brief and supplied selects.
disable-model-invocation: true
---


Read the job brief at $ARGUMENTS. If no path is supplied, ask for it.
Resolve paths in the brief relative to the project root.


## Scope and defaults


Use only the brief's named sources and allowed source-relative ranges.
Do not search for substitute footage or reuse another job's inputs.
Preserve source audio with its picture. Do not remove pauses or filler
words automatically, change speech speed, or mute audio by default.
Ask before adding music, generated assets, or unapproved copy.


Default export: MP4, H.264 video, AAC audio, 1280x720, 16:9.
Use the brief's frame rate; otherwise propose one after inspecting sources.
Explicit job requirements override editorial and export defaults.
Missing or contradictory requirements need clarification.


Never modify source files or overwrite an existing output.
Keep every job's artifacts in its own work and output directories.


## Plan before rendering


Read the brief and inspect named sources using permitted tools.
Confirm files, durations, audio streams, ranges, and available renderer.
If a tool, permission, or required input is missing, explain and stop.
Do not install software or connect services as part of this skill.


Save a proposed cut plan in the job's work directory.
For each segment, record source identity (path and checksum), source-relative
in/out points, timeline placement, audio treatment, and framing.
State time units and endpoint convention. Record copy, export settings,
expected duration, renderer, and intended output path.
Flag uncertainties and any requested departure from defaults.


Present the plan and wait for explicit approval before rendering.
Preserve the approved plan and approval record. Revisions need new approval.


## Render and review


Render only the approved plan with available, permitted tools.
Retain the render script or commands, logs, approved plan, source mapping,
and output path in the job directory.
Inspect output metadata against the plan. Report completed checks,
failures, and anything requiring human playback review.
Do not claim an editable NLE project unless one was actually created.
Save review notes beside the plan; version revisions without overwriting.


```


[Keep supporting references](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#add-supporting-files) beside the skill if it grows. A caption specification could live at` .claude/skills/edit-review-cut/references/captions.md` , with an instruction in` SKILL.md` to read it when captions are requested. Don’t add reference files just to make the folder look complete, because this starter works without them.


## Give each video its own brief


For a first trial, use a couple of short sample clips. You can[download the sample project accompanying this guide](https://cdn.aspectlabs.dev/blog/claude-code-video-editing-skill/edit-review-cut-sample-436227e948f2.zip) , which includes this skill, two briefs, and two synthetic clips with different colors and tones. Save your brief as` jobs/sample/brief.md` . When you use your own footage, change the filenames and ranges to match it.


```text
Job: sample review cut
All paths are relative to the project root.
Work directory: jobs/sample/work/
Output: jobs/sample/outputs/review-v01.mp4


Sources and selects, in sequence:
- media/sample/intro.mp4: 00:00:02.000 to 00:00:08.000
- media/sample/detail.mp4: 00:00:01.000 to 00:00:07.000


Ranges are source-relative elapsed time, start inclusive, end exclusive.
Use both ranges in full, with a straight cut between them.
Expected duration: 12 seconds.


Target: 9:16, 1080x1920, 30 fps.
Fit the entire image with black padding; do not crop.
Keep each select's original audio. No music or generated material.
Approved on-screen copy: none. No captions.


Use the skill's default codec settings.
Retain the approved plan, source mapping, render commands, and review notes.


```


The portrait dimensions deliberately override the skill’s landscape default. The framing instruction also resolves a separate decision: portrait output doesn't necessarily mean cropping landscape footage.


Open Claude Code at the project root, then invoke:


```text
/edit-review-cut jobs/sample/brief.md


```


If Claude Code doesn't recognize the command, confirm the directory, the exact` SKILL.md` filename, and the YAML metadata. Fix discovery before troubleshooting the renderer. If the skill loads but Claude Code can't render because it lacks an executable or permission, that's a tool-access problem, not a reason to rewrite your editing preferences.


## Approve the cut plan


Review the proposed cuts and framing before rendering.


For the example brief, the first source's 2–8 second range belongs at timeline 0–6 seconds. The second source's 1–7 second range belongs at timeline 6–12 seconds. Keep both source and timeline times in the plan so a note such as “restore the beginning of the second shot” points to the right footage.


Source time identifies the part of the original clip. Timeline time identifies where that selection appears in your edit. This diagram shows the two ranges in the sample brief. Read the plan for editorial consequences, not just valid syntax. Does it preserve both audio streams? Does “fit” mean padding rather than a center crop? Did it invent a title because the result seemed sparse? A plausible-looking plan can still contradict the brief.


Once it matches your intent, approve that saved version explicitly:


```text
Approve jobs/sample/work/cut-plan-v01.md.
Render that plan to the stated output path.
If anything requires changing the plan, stop and ask.


```


The retained commands or script make the export easier to reproduce, but they aren't automatically an editable timeline. If you need an NLE project, specify the required format in the brief and confirm that your connected tool can actually produce it.


## Try a second brief


Use the small sample to exercise the workflow, not to judge your whole production setup.


First, confirm that manual invocation loads the skill and produces a plan without rendering. Then make a second job brief with a different output directory and landscape dimensions. Check that its plan changes the export geometry while preserving rules such as supplied-selects-only and original audio.


That comparison exposes a common failure: a value from the previous job becoming an accidental default. If the second plan still points to the first output path, stop there.


When the tools and permissions allow a sample render, play it back. Metadata can confirm[dimensions, codec, and duration](https://ffmpeg.org/ffprobe.html) ; it can't tell you whether a word ending feels clipped or the transition sounds abrupt. Listen across the cut and compare the beginning and end of each select with its source. Keep the findings with that job’s artifacts.


We ran the sample with Claude Code 2.1.330 and FFmpeg 8.1.2 on November 23, 2026. Claude loaded the skill, produced separate portrait and landscape plans, and waited for approval before rendering. Both outputs contained 360 frames over 12 seconds, with H.264 video and AAC audio. Their dimensions matched the two briefs: 1080×1920 and 1280×720. The source files stayed unchanged.


The clips contain flat colors and test tones, so this demonstrates following a brief and producing the requested files. It doesn't demonstrate choosing a good performance or cutting dialogue naturally. Download the[portrait output](https://cdn.aspectlabs.dev/blog/claude-code-video-editing-skill/portrait-review-6f14f9464fe1.mp4) or[landscape output](https://cdn.aspectlabs.dev/blog/claude-code-video-editing-skill/landscape-review-761ab59f4a08.mp4) to watch and listen to them.


## Save feedback you want to reuse


Suppose the owner says, “At six seconds, you cut off the inhale that makes the next sentence feel natural.”


Record the six-second timestamp in this job’s review notes. A reusable instruction might be: “Preserve breaths that lead into speech; if an approved select boundary clips one, flag it and request an expanded range rather than silently extending the select.”


That rule explains the preference and respects source boundaries. “Never cut at six seconds” does neither.


Ask whether feedback applies to this edit, this series, or every edit using the skill. Update the brief for a one-off correction. Update the skill only when the owner confirms a repeatable preference. Version both so your team can explain why a later edit behaves differently.


Your Claude Code skill stays separate: saving` SKILL.md` doesn't automatically install or synchronize it into Aspect, or control Aspect without a separately connected tool.


[Keep the skill with the project](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#share-skills) so your team can reuse the same editing instructions on the next video.


## Frequently Asked Questions


Put repeatable editing instructions in the skill, such as preserving source audio, using only supplied selects, and waiting for plan approval. Put each video's source paths, allowed ranges, sequence, approved copy, and output requirements in its brief. Explicit job requirements can override export defaults, but shouldn't bypass safeguards such as leaving source files untouched.


Save the instructions in .claude/skills/edit-review-cut/SKILL.md under your project root, with YAML metadata defining the name and description. Set disable-model-invocation: true to prevent automatic invocation. Then run /edit-review-cut jobs/sample/brief.md in Claude Code. Manual invocation doesn't replace tool permissions or explicit approval of the cut plan.


No. A skill supplies instructions, not media-processing capabilities. Claude Code still needs access to a suitable renderer or connected editing tool, along with permission to use it. If a required executable, connection, or input is missing, the workflow should stop and explain the blocker rather than install software or connect services automatically.


Not automatically. A rendered MP4, saved commands, and a cut plan can support reproduction and revision, but they aren't an editable NLE project. If you need a timeline, name the required project or interchange format in the brief and confirm that the available tool can generate it. Test the resulting import in your target NLE.


Keep the project-scoped skill in a shared, version-controlled repository while giving every job its own brief, work directory, and output directory. Don't embed client filenames or select timestamps in the reusable instructions. Record which skill version and approved plan each render used, and keep confidential media and credentials out of the repository unless your team's access and storage policies explicitly allow them.


Aspect’s agent applies[saved brand Skills](https://aspect.inc/product/agent) across creative jobs, keeping reusable colors and visual direction available as teammates develop assets. Keep each video’s source selections in its own Claude Code brief, and maintain the editing skill separately: saving a local SKILL.md doesn't automatically synchronize it with Aspect.
